description: The IXP Database (IXPDB) is a live public source of data about internet exchange points, run by Euro-IX, the association of European exchanges. Instead of relying on manual entries it collects data automatically from exchanges' own management systems through the IX-F member export format, to give an accurate, current view of the interconnection landscape. It holds data on exchange architecture, locations, member networks, switching hardware, port capacity and traffic utilisation, and the site lists the largest exchanges by member count with the time of each automatic import (for example IX.br São Paulo, LINX LON1, NAPAfrica Johannesburg and MSK-IX, imported on 24 to 26 September 2026). Coverage is worldwide wherever exchanges publish an IX-F export, strongest in Europe and among Euro-IX member and affiliate exchanges; on 26 September 2026 the public API's provider list returned 1,134 entries. Access is through the website and a documented public REST API returning JSON, with no fee; use is bound by the IXPDB acceptable use policy, and the site states all rights reserved. Uses named by the provider include commercial analysis, network automation and historical benchmarking. Caveats: exchanges that do not publish IX-F exports are missing or thin, traffic figures depend on what exchanges share, and the database shows where interconnection is offered, not traffic paths. Simulation uses: exchange locations, members and capacities for internet interconnection network models, capacity planning and cascading-failure and resilience studies. Related records: PeeringDB and the PCH Internet Exchange Point Directory.
